answer: Make identity itself scarce and priced. Each epoch the network mints a fixed delta of new agent licenses by sealed-bid auction; the winning bond locks for a year and is drawn down if that license joins a collusive cluster. The price curve is velvet-smooth but steep: the hundredth license in a batch costs far more than the first, so bulk registration front-loads cost instead of hiding it. An attacker must win N bids and freeze N slashable bonds that earn nothing, while an honest newcomer pays one small bond. Crystal-clear accounting keeps the premium auditable, and fixed supply caps growth.
